critical.issue: The 502 status is correct and backend emits detail 'Payment gateway authentication failed…' (verified against localhost:8001). HOWEVER the Cloudflare/Emergent edge proxy STRIPS the body of every 5xx response and substitutes its own HTML 502 Bad Gateway page. Through the preview URL the client only receives Cloudflare HTML — the specific message is lost. Reproduction: curl -X POST https://memories-album.preview.emergentagent.com/api/payments/razorpay/order (with a valid customer token + unpaid order_id) → status 502, content-type text/html, body is Cloudflare error page; while curl against http://localhost:8001 returns the JSON detail. Fix: return a non-5xx HTTP status (e.g. 400 Bad Request or 422 Unprocessable Entity, or 200 with {error}) so the body passes through the edge, OR explicitly map this condition to 400 in payments router. The spec called for 502, but it is not achievable on the production edge.

ui_bugs.issue: When /api/payments/razorpay/order returns 502, the UI inserts the ENTIRE raw HTML 502 body (<!DOCTYPE html>...<title>preview.emergentagent.com | 502: Bad gateway</title>…) into the DELIVERY DETAILS section of the checkout page instead of rendering a clean error message. There is no visible [data-testid="checkout-error"] element; users see broken HTML text and no clear 'Payment failed' feedback.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend expects a clean JSON {detail} body on 502. Backend emits it, but the Cloudflare edge replaces it with HTML before it reaches the browser, so the frontend's onError path uses the raw HTML as the error message. Fix either (a) backend status (use 4xx) OR (b) frontend: on 502/5xx with non-JSON body, substitute a generic 'Payment temporarily unavailable. Please try again.' message and render it via a visible checkout-error element.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Edge-level 5xx body stripping: Cloudflare/Emergent ingress REPLACES the body of any 5xx response with its own HTML error page while preserving the status code. Any backend endpoint that intentionally returns 502/503 with a structured JSON {detail: ...} must change to 4xx (or 200 with error payload) if the message is meant to reach the browser. rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE for the 'blank/garbled checkout screen' issue: FastAPI correctly raises HTTPException(502, 'Could not start payment: Payment gateway authentication failed. The Razorpay API keys configured on the server are invalid …'). Status 502 is passed up through the ingress, BUT Cloudflare/Emergent's edge intercepts 5xx responses and substitutes an HTML 502 Bad Gateway page as the response body (content-type text/html). The frontend's razorpay-checkout.tsx reads response.text() or JSON-parses, finds HTML, and renders it verbatim. Net effect: user sees <!DOCTYPE html>... garbage mid-checkout instead of the clean error. Mitigation A (preferred, 1-line change): switch to HTTPException(400 or 422, ...) in payments.py:45 so Cloudflare lets the body through. Mitigation B (frontend hardening): in the Pay-Now error handler, detect text/html Content-Type (or 'preview.emergentagent.com | 502' in body) and fall back to a canned 'Payment gateway temporarily unavailable, please try again.' rendered via a dedicated [data-testid="checkout-error"] component. Ship BOTH for defence in depth.
